questions.text: Why does Reciprocal Rank Fusion use ranking positions rather than adding raw BM25 and vector similarity scores?

options.A: To guarantee that every relevant document appears in the fused results.
options.B: To combine results without requiring the two score scales to be comparable.
options.C: To discard documents that appear in only one retrieval method.
options.D: To remove the need to rank documents within either retrieval method.

questions.explanation: RRF sums reciprocal-rank contributions, allowing fusion across retrieval methods whose raw scores have different scales.

questions.text: A short passage matches a query precisely but lacks surrounding conditions needed to answer it. Which strategy directly addresses this retrieval-versus-context tradeoff?

options.A: Search child chunks, then include their larger parent chunks in the prompt.
options.B: Search child chunks, then remove all surrounding text before generation.
options.C: Increase sampling temperature while keeping the same incomplete passage.
options.D: Use a hypothetical answer as verified evidence without retrieving documents.

questions.explanation: Parent-child retrieval matches smaller passages while supplying their larger parent sections as generation context.

questions.text: The toy evaluate_faithfulness function keeps only sentences whose stripped length is greater than 10. If none remain, it returns (1.0, []). What does it return for answer="No." with no retrieved chunks?

options.A: (0.0, ["No"]), because the answer has no supporting source.
options.B: (0.0, []), because an empty context always scores zero.
options.C: (1.0, []), because the short sentence is excluded before checking support.
options.D: It raises ValueError because the retrieved context is empty.

questions.explanation: "No" has length 2 after splitting on periods, so it is filtered out. The early return gives 1.0 without checking any claim; this does not establish actual faithfulness.
